direction_as_read: positive_weak: migraine prevention with Petadolex root extract at 150 mg/day; 100 mg/day was not significant in the larger trial, and no other preparation on these labels was tested
summary: Efficacy is specific to one material and one purpose. Two adult RCTs of the root extract Petadolex report fewer migraine attacks: the larger at 150 mg/day but not 100 mg/day (15623680), and a small trial at 100 mg/day whose reanalysis notes major shortcomings (14752215). Reviews call the evidence moderate (16987643) or positive but limited (32310327), not strong. A small child trial is null after treatment and positive at follow-up (17659990). Only 3 of 25 labels name Petadolex. No trial of whole-herb extract was found, and 6 labels print it.
question_for_clinician: Two adult RCTs support Petadolex at 150 mg/day for migraine, yet 22 of 25 labels aren't Petadolex and the liver items on clinician_items are unresolved. Should any label get credit? Agent recommendation: no credit, with direction at most positive_weak, Petadolex root extract only.
